options_evaluated: Virgin plastics with complex internal ribbing
assessments.rationale: Using recycled mono-materials with simplified molding minimizes the manufacturing environmental footprint (m) and energy/resource consumption in production (g) compared to virgin plastics or energy-intensive aluminum. It also reduces plastic waste generated during the molding process (r) and minimizes the release of microplastics and nanoplastics (p) during cutting and finishing. Page 33 notes that ecodesign requirements aim to improve environmental impacts, including carbon footprint and environmental footprint (parameter m), and expected generation of waste (parameter r). Page 80 also highlights the need to minimize amounts of waste generated (r) and microplastic/nanoplastic release during manufacturing (p).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation stage (durability and mechanical strength might be lower than virgin plastics or metal, leading to shorter product life).

assessments.rationale: Mechanical fasteners avoid volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions to air, water, or soil (q) and hazardous waste generation (r) associated with chemical adhesives and solvents. Page 3 calls for a 'Zero Pollution for Air, Water and Soil' and a 'toxic-free environment' in production, while Page 80 (q) and (r) mandate addressing emissions to air, water, or soil and amounts of waste generated (including hazardous waste) during manufacturing.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation stage (potential air leaks lowering suction efficiency compared to hermetically sealed adhesive joints).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with rare-earth magnets
assessments.rationale: Manufacturing motors with rare-earth magnets involves highly energy-intensive extraction and refining, which increases resource consumption in production (g), manufacturing environmental footprint (m), and releases significant toxic emissions to air, water, and soil (q). Page 3 outlines the commitment to 'zero pollution ambition in production' and Page 80 (q) emphasizes minimizing emissions to air, water, or soil released in manufacturing.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation stage (brushless motors with rare-earth magnets offer higher energy efficiency and power density, so avoiding them may decrease use-phase efficiency).

options_evaluated: Active cooling fan integrated into motor shaft
Passive heat sinks with thermal interface materials (TIMs)
assessments.recommendation: Active cooling fan integrated into motor shaft
assessments.rationale: Integrating the cooling fan directly into the motor shaft reduces material consumption and avoids the need for separate thermal interface materials (TIMs) or complex heat sinks. This minimizes resource consumption in production (g) and manufacturing environmental footprint (m), as well as waste generation (r) in line with Page 33 (environmental impacts and expected generation of waste) and Page 80 (r) (amounts of waste generated).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation stage (may increase noise emissions (q) [Page 80] and provide less optimal cooling than dedicated heat sinks, potentially reducing motor lifespan).

options_evaluated: Modular component blocks with plug-and-play connectors
Standardized internal layout with discrete components
assessments.rationale: From a manufacturing-only perspective, a monolithic design simplifies the assembly line, requiring fewer separate manufacturing steps, less energy and resource consumption in production (g), and generates less manufacturing waste (r) and lower carbon footprint in production (m) compared to complex modular architectures. Page 33 and Page 80 (r) emphasize minimizing waste generation and environmental footprint.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation and End-of-life stages (highly integrated monolithic designs severely restrict repairability, upgradability, and component recovery/recyclability, which are key circularity aspects mentioned on Page 3 and Page 33).

assessments.rationale: A corded AC power supply avoids the high energy, water, and resource consumption (g) and environmental footprint (m) of manufacturing lithium-ion batteries. It also eliminates toxic emissions to air, water, and soil (q) and hazardous waste (r) generated during battery production. Page 3 calls for a 'toxic-free environment' and 'zero pollution ambition in production,' and Page 80 (q) and (r) target emissions and hazardous waste in manufacturing.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use/Operation stage (limits portability and user convenience, and may affect use-phase energy efficiency compared to low-voltage DC battery-operated motors).
